newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan May long-term prime rate seen higher - traders.
newsitem.headline: Japan May long-term prime rate seen higher - traders.

text.p: Japan's long-term prime rate is likely to be raised to around 3.1 or 3.2 percent in May from 2.5 percent in April, bond traders said on Friday.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd's (IBJ) 1.60 percent five-year bank debenture issued in April was last traded at 2.3 percent on Friday, up sharply from Thursday's 2.03 percent, traders said.
Judging from current market conditions, the coupon rates for the IBJ's May bank debentures and its May long-term prime rate are likely to be raised by 0.6 or 0.7 percentage point, bond traders said.
An IBJ spokesman said the bank would announce its long-term prime lending rate for May next Monday.

The prime rate, at which long-term credit banks lend to their most creditworthy customers, was cut by 0.2 percentage point to a record low 2.5 percent in December and has remained unchanged since then.
The IBJ customarily sets its long-term prime rate 0.9 percentage point above its five-year bank debenture coupon rate.
